s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal syndrome with gastric distension and duodenal compression
salient_findings: Compression of the third portion of the duodenum between the superior mesenteric artery and the aorta
key_facts: Progressive inability to tolerate oral intake
Marked gastric distension on abdominal ultrasonography and plain radiographs
Normal upper gastrointestinal endoscopy with no intrinsic luminal lesions
Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen revealed compression of the third portion of the duodenum

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal syndrome with gastric distension and duodenal compression
salient_findings: Compression of the third portion of the duodenum between the superior mesenteric artery and the aorta
key_facts: Progressive inability to tolerate oral intake
Marked gastric distension on abdominal ultrasonography and plain radiographs
Normal upper gastrointestinal endoscopy with no intrinsic luminal lesions
Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen revealed compression of the third portion of the duodenum

shortlist.label: Superior mesenteric artery syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Compression of the third portion of the duodenum between the superior mesenteric artery and the aorta at an acute angle, consistent with CT findings

shortlist.label: Gastric outlet obstruction
shortlist.why_kept: Intractable vomiting, postprandial upper abdominal pain, and bloating, with marked gastric distension on imaging

shortlist.label: Vascular compression syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Reduced aortomesenteric angle and compression of the duodenum, supported by CT findings

shortlist.label: Median arcuate ligament syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of duodenal compression, given the patient's lean body habitus and history of fasting

shortlist.label: Celiac artery compression syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of abdominal pain and bloating, although less likely given the specific CT findings

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of intractable vomiting, postprandial upper abdominal pain, and bloating, combined with the CT findings of compression of the third portion of the duodenum between the superior mesenteric artery and the aorta, are consistent with Superior mesenteric artery syndrome.

rejected.label: Gastric outlet obstruction
rejected.why: Normal upper gastrointestinal endoscopy with no intrinsic luminal lesions makes this less likely

rejected.label: Vascular compression syndrome
rejected.why: While this is a broader category, the specific findings point more directly to Superior mesenteric artery syndrome

rejected.label: Median arcuate ligament syndrome
rejected.why: This condition involves compression of the celiac artery, which is not indicated in the provided CT findings

rejected.label: Celiac artery compression syndrome
rejected.why: The CT findings specifically mention compression of the duodenum between the superior mesenteric artery and the aorta, not the celiac artery
